## The wind-down announcement (July 2012)

**"Fortress Wrapping Up"**, posted by Guy Steele ("gls"), July 20, 2012 —
[snapshot 2012-10-07](https://web.archive.org/web/20121007034544/https://blogs.oracle.com/projectfortress/entry/fortress_wrapping_up);
a [2016 capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20160924201206/https://blogs.oracle.com/projectfortress/entry/fortress_wrapping_up)
additionally preserves 17 reader comments. This post is the entire
announcement — there was no separate wind-down FAQ. Key sentences:

> "After working nearly a decade on the design, development, and
> implementation of the Fortress programming language, the Oracle Labs
> Programming Language Research Group is now winding down the Fortress
> project. Ten years is a remarkably long run for an industrial research
> project (one to three years is much more typical)..."

> "...we encountered some severe technical challenges having to do with
> the mismatch between the (rather ambitious) Fortress type system and a
> virtual machine not designed to support it (that would be every
> currently available VM, not just JVM)."

> "The Fortress source code remains open-source, and the code repository
> will remain available for the foreseeable future."

The post credits Chapel, X10, Clojure, and Scala as "friendly
competition", lists **eight aspects "we are quite pleased with"**
(generators/reducers; work-stealing implicit parallelism; nested atomic
blocks on transactional memory; non-erased parametric polymorphism;
symmetric multimethod dispatch; symmetric multiple inheritance with type
exclusion; mathematical syntax and juxtaposition; components and APIs)
and **three "wish we had explored further"** (dimensions and units;
explicit data distribution / processor assignment; conditional
inheritance via `where` clauses). Press echo: SD Times, *"Fortress
Finally Folds"*, July 24, 2012.

## Community and site mechanics

- Trac-based site with open registration; tickets doubled as
  language-change proposals; anonymous SVN
  (`svn checkout https://projectfortress.sun.com/svn/Community/trunk PFC`);
  contributions required a faxed Sun Contributor Agreement. "Project
  Fortress is led by the Programming Language Research Group of Sun

\section{Operator Precedence and Associativity}
\seclabel{operator-precedence}

Fortress specifies that certain operators have higher precedence than
certain other operators and certain operators are associative,
so that one need not use parentheses in all
cases where operators are mixed in an expression.  (See
\appref{operator-precedence} for a detailed description of operator
precedence and associativity in Fortress.)  However, Fortress
does not follow the practice of other programming languages in
simply assigning an integer to each operator and then saying that
the precedence of any two operators can be compared by comparing
their assigned integers.  Instead, Fortress relies on defining traditional
groups of operators based on their meaning and shape, and specifies
specific precedence relationships between some of these groups.
If there is no specific precedence relationship between two
operators, then parentheses must be used.  For example, Fortress
does not accept the expression \EXP{a + b \cup c};
one must write either \EXP{(a + b) \cup c} or \EXP{a + (b \cup c)}.
(Whether or not the result then makes any sense depends on what definitions
have been made for the \EXP{+} and \EXP{\cup} operators---see
\chapref{operatordefs}.)

Here are the basic principles of operator precedence and associativity
in Fortress:

\begin{itemize}
\item
Member selection (\txt{.}) and method invocation
(\EXP{.\VAR{name}(\ldots)}) are not operators.  They have higher precedence
than any operator listed below.

\item
Subscripting (\txt{[ ]} and any kind of subscripting operators,
which can be any kind of enclosing operators),
superscripting (\txt{{\char'136}}),
and postfix operators have higher precedence than any operator
listed below; within this group, these operations are left-associative
(performed left-to-right).

<!-- Fourth part of the territory map, written by a survey worker before the historical source tree is opened for modification. Question: for each design area of the language, where is the rationale written down. Method: read the sources in this repository; no external fetches; no PDFs or decks added to the tree. Every checkable claim cites file:line or a URL already in research/README.md. -->

# Where the design intent is written down

The specification says what the language is, not why; the why sits in five places, and this file says which place holds which area.

The five places: `Papers/` (five in-repo paper directories, four of them buildable); the Guy Steele corpus indexed by `research/README.md` (links, plus per-session local copies under the gitignored `research/decks/`); `research/extracts/` (our committed working notes on those sources); the specification's own draft-only apparatus (the `\note{}` boxes and the Internal Document appendix, both suppressed in release builds); and the source tree itself (tool docs, long design comments, aspirational test directories, commit messages).

Two structural facts to carry into the rest of this file.

The rationale that is in the specification is in the *draft* build only: `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex:24-37` defines `\note` as empty when `\release` is set, and `Specification/appendices/appendices.tex:24-26` includes the Internal Document chapter only in the non-release build; "Internal Document" appears 0 times in the text of the published `Specification-1.0-frozen/fortress.1.0.pdf` and twice in the in-repo draft render `Specification/fortress.pdf` (599 pages), which also carries 36 occurrences of the editorial "Victor:" notes that the 1.0 PDF has none of.

The deepest layer of the design record is *not* in the repository: 27 `\note{}` passages point at Sun-internal email threads by subject and date (`grep -rn 'email titled' Specification --include='*.tex'`, e.g. `Specification/appendices/future.tex:65`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:28`, `Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:17`), and `research/README.md:110-113` records that no archive of the project mailing lists was found anywhere as of 2026-08-21.

## 4. The specification itself

Searching the LaTeX for the word "rationale" finds exactly one passage, and it is about component upgrade, not about the language: `Specification/basic/components/basic.tex:372`.

The rationale the spec does carry is in four other forms.

`Specification/preliminaries/intro/philosophy.tex:12-40` is the design-goals statement: a growable language, "secure Fortran", the list of languages Fortress borrowed from; `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:88-95` is the one place the spec explicitly motivates a design decision ("These design decisions are motivated in part by our goal of making the scientist/programmer's life as easy as possible…").

The 230 `\note{}` boxes are the implementers' margin: they are draft-only, and they range from status ("not yet supported") to open argument. Distribution by file, highest first: `basic/lexical-structure.tex` 19, `basic/traits.tex` 15, `basic/types-vals-vars.tex` 14, `basic/memory-model.tex` 9, `basic/expressions/literals.tex` 9, `basic/declarations.tex` 9, `basic/components/source-code.tex` 9, `basic/functions.tex` 7, `basic/components/intro.tex` 7, `basic/objects.tex` 6, `advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex` 6, `preliminaries/overview.tex` 5, `basic/tests.tex` 5, `basic/dimensions.tex` 5, then 4 or fewer in `basic/matrix-unpasting.tex`, `basic/expressions/typecase.tex`, `basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex`, `basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `basic/trait-parameters.tex`, `basic/overloading.tex`, `basic/operators/opr-fixity.tex`, `basic/evaluation/values.tex`, `basic/evaluation/reduction.tex`, `appendices/ascii-to-unicode.tex`, `advanced/parallelism-locality/shared-local.tex`, `advanced/overloading.tex`, and others.

The substantive ones, as samples: `basic/memory-model.tex:439-441` ("The following is controversial. I think this is effectively the condition the X10 guys are trying to capture formally…") and `:376-379` ("The following doesn't fully address Bill Pugh's concerns…"); `basic/dimensions.tex:244-254`, Guy's explanation that unit information is static and is omitted from the run-time representation exactly when type information is; `basic/conversions-coercions.tex:19-37`, an open-questions list for coercion including tests, tuple and arrow types; `basic/traits.tex:174-182` and `:195-197`, Victor's observation that a trait can explicitly extend itself through hidden type variables.

`Specification/appendices/internal-document.tex` is the spec's own rationale appendix, included only in draft builds, and it inputs two files: `appendices/FAQ.tex` (235 lines of answered design questions — why multiple dispatch rather than single, `:59`; why spawn counts as IO, `:51`; core versus standard library, `:121`; why not single inheritance between objects, `:136`; juxtaposition as the only non-ALLCAPS operator name, `:90`) and `appendices/future.tex` (756 lines of proposed features organised as Syntax and Evaluation, Types, Traits and Objects, Functions and Overloading, Expressions, Operators and Coercions, Exceptions, Components and APIs, Others, Tools — largely a digest of meetings and emails, with the participants named and their positions recorded, e.g. the array/tensor discussion at `:63-76`).

The formal apparatus is the fourth form: `Specification/appendices/calculi/` holds four core calculi (basic, `where`, overloading, acffd — `appendices/calculi/calculi.tex:18-21`), and `appendices/overloading-function.tex:12` and `appendices/overloading-coercion.tex:12` are the proofs that the overloading rules admit no ambiguous or undefined call, and that coercion resolution is well defined.

`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/FAQ.tex` and `future.tex` are byte-identical to the draft's (diff), so the frozen tree adds nothing here; what differs is that the release build hides them.

`Documentation/Specification/` is a second, later, partial spec source tree in Fortify `.tick` form (build instructions at `Documentation/Specification/Prose/README.txt:12-24`, directory roles at `Documentation/Specification/README.txt:13-25`), carrying 35 `\note{}` passages of its own; its committed render `Documentation/Specification/fortress.pdf` is 65 pages, built 2012-05-31, against the draft tree's 599.

## 5. Design notes inside the source tree

Prose documents that state design, not usage: `Fortify/fortify-doc.txt` (489 lines, the Emacs-based ASCII-to-typeset conversion and the identifier-to-symbol rules) with `Fortify/example/README`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/parser-doc.txt` (98 lines, the Rats! module structure of the grammar, with NYI markers); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/syntax_abstractions/productionsAndAst.txt` (127 lines, which productions a user grammar may extend — "Only those marked \"x\" can be extended currently"); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser_util/precedence_resolver/operators.txt` (1,093 lines, the operator groups by meaning and shape that the precedence relation is built from); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/README` (the linker's purpose and file-by-file map); `BasicCoreFortress/README.txt` (how to run the core-calculus interpreter); root `README.txt` (the Subversion-era orientation, describing a project layout that no longer holds).

Long comments that explain a design choice rather than a mechanism, found by scanning every `/* … */` block of 14 lines or more under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/{compiler,scala_src,runtimeSystem,interpreter}`: `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:26-35` (why a task is not forked in its constructor — "Given the plethora of final fields in the usual Fortress task, such a step would be a memory model disaster!"); `compiler/NamingCzar.java:264-289` (the six-level ladder from a Fortress name to an ASM type, and the two translations needed for foreign interfaces); `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:869-906` (why forwarding methods are generated for every trait after the first, and the normalized-inheritance assumption it rests on), `:1015-1049`, `:1147-1183`, `:2313-2340`, `:5161-5196` (RTTI classes); `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:53-56` ("This code steals willy-nilly from the NextGen class loader"), `:532-552`, `:690-721`, `:935-957` (how arrow and tuple interfaces are synthesized on demand), `:1181-1202`; `runtimeSystem/Naming.java:13-16` (why this class must not depend on the compiler); `runtimeSystem/InstantiationMap.java:195-224` (the name-rewriting state machine); `interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:31-68` ("This comment is not yet true; it is a goal."); `interpreter/evaluator/transactions/manager/KarmaManager.java:17-37` and `EruptionManager.java:17-42` (two of eleven contention-management policies, each with its heuristic explained).

Only one comment in the whole source tree uses the word "rationale" (`interpreter/glue/prim/Reflect.java:333`), and only four say "we chose / we decided / the reason" in any form (`interpreter/evaluator/transactions/manager/FortressManager5.java:22`, `interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:849`, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2206`, plus the Reflect one); intent in this tree is expressed as mechanism, and 556 `TODO` markers carry what is left of the "not yet" record.

The aspirational test directories are themselves a statement of intent — what was meant to work and did not: `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet` (62 files, e.g. `WhereConstraints.fss`, `UnitExpr.fss`, `Expr.Array.Pasting.fss`, `XXXextendOprParam1.fss`), `long_term_not_working` (6: abstract, closures, fields, inheritance, overriding, wordcount), `not_working_static_tests` (43), `not_working_library_tests` (29), `not_working_compiler_tests` (10), `obsolete_interpreter_tests` (3).

Commit messages: sampled with `git log --grep` over the historical era (`--until=2013-01-01`), they are overwhelmingly implementation logs, and design statements appear in them only in passing — the clearest samples are `128f313b5` (2009-11-17, jmaessen: coercion of `IntLiteral` by `ZZ32`, "as we gradually migrate to a flat numeric hierarchy"), `8e3968ea7` (2009-11-11, skilpat: coercions from union types "as per Guy's blog post" — the blog post is not in the repo), `c35aac139` (2012-04-24, David Chase: "Preliminary disabling of contravariance (in overloaded dispatch)", the retreat the JuliaCon deck describes at slide 44), `32153798d` (2008-04-27, jmaessen: a juxtaposition/type-inference fix that "opened a rift in space-time"), `821e29621` (2008-02-07: BIG operators implemented, "'BIG juxtaposition' is PROD not PRODUCT").

Caveat on that sampling: path-scoped history is unreliable in this repository — `research/authorship.md:14-22` records that the hg→git conversion severed 146 parent links, so `git log -- <path>` dead-ends (it reports one commit for `Papers/`), while `git log --full-history --all -- <path>` over-reports (404 commits for `Papers/`, most of which do not touch it). The `--grep` samples above walk all commits and are sound as samples; they are not an exhaustive search.

Whether `Papers/Implementation` should be made buildable — the missing `FortressEncodings.tex` could be reconstructed as a wrapper around the two existing documents, but that is an edit inside the sealed tree and is the owner's call.

Whether the specification's draft-only apparatus (the `\note{}` boxes and the Internal Document appendix) should be surfaced as a first-class revival document, given that it is the richest rationale source in the repository and is invisible to anyone reading the published 1.0 PDF.

Whether to pursue the lost email record — the 27 named threads are the primary rationale source for coercion, overloading, arrays, tuples, fairness and function equality, and recovering even one thread would change what several rows above can say.

Whether `research/README.md` should index the two APL deck files now sitting in `research/decks/`, which belong to a different line of work.

Whether the aspirational test directories (`not_passing_yet`, `long_term_not_working`, and the three `not_working_*`) should be read as a design-intent source in their own right and cross-referenced to the gap ledger.

# Where the design intent is written down

The specification says what the language is, not why; the why sits in five places, and this file says which place holds which area.

The five places: `Papers/` (five in-repo paper directories, four of them buildable); the Guy Steele corpus indexed by `research/README.md` (links, plus per-session local copies under the gitignored `research/decks/`); `research/extracts/` (our committed working notes on those sources); the specification's own draft-only apparatus (the `\note{}` boxes and the Internal Document appendix, both suppressed in release builds); and the source tree itself (tool docs, long design comments, aspirational test directories, commit messages).

Two structural facts to carry into the rest of this file.

The rationale that is in the specification is in the *draft* build only: `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex:24-37` defines `\note` as empty when `\release` is set, and `Specification/appendices/appendices.tex:24-26` includes the Internal Document chapter only in the non-release build; "Internal Document" appears 0 times in the text of the published `Specification-1.0-frozen/fortress.1.0.pdf` and twice in the in-repo draft render `Specification/fortress.pdf` (599 pages), which also carries 36 occurrences of the editorial "Victor:" notes that the 1.0 PDF has none of.

The deepest layer of the design record is *not* in the repository: 27 `\note{}` passages point at Sun-internal email threads by subject and date (`grep -rn 'email titled' Specification --include='*.tex'`, e.g. `Specification/appendices/future.tex:65`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:28`, `Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:17`), and `research/README.md:110-113` records that no archive of the project mailing lists was found anywhere as of 2026-08-21.

## 4. The specification itself

Searching the LaTeX for the word "rationale" finds exactly one passage, and it is about component upgrade, not about the language: `Specification/basic/components/basic.tex:372`.

The rationale the spec does carry is in four other forms.

`Specification/preliminaries/intro/philosophy.tex:12-40` is the design-goals statement: a growable language, "secure Fortran", the list of languages Fortress borrowed from; `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:88-95` is the one place the spec explicitly motivates a design decision ("These design decisions are motivated in part by our goal of making the scientist/programmer's life as easy as possible…").

The 230 `\note{}` boxes are the implementers' margin: they are draft-only, and they range from status ("not yet supported") to open argument. Distribution by file, highest first: `basic/lexical-structure.tex` 19, `basic/traits.tex` 15, `basic/types-vals-vars.tex` 14, `basic/memory-model.tex` 9, `basic/expressions/literals.tex` 9, `basic/declarations.tex` 9, `basic/components/source-code.tex` 9, `basic/functions.tex` 7, `basic/components/intro.tex` 7, `basic/objects.tex` 6, `advanced/parallelism-locality/defining-generators.tex` 6, `preliminaries/overview.tex` 5, `basic/tests.tex` 5, `basic/dimensions.tex` 5, then 4 or fewer in `basic/matrix-unpasting.tex`, `basic/expressions/typecase.tex`, `basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex`, `basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `basic/trait-parameters.tex`, `basic/overloading.tex`, `basic/operators/opr-fixity.tex`, `basic/evaluation/values.tex`, `basic/evaluation/reduction.tex`, `appendices/ascii-to-unicode.tex`, `advanced/parallelism-locality/shared-local.tex`, `advanced/overloading.tex`, and others.

The substantive ones, as samples: `basic/memory-model.tex:439-441` ("The following is controversial. I think this is effectively the condition the X10 guys are trying to capture formally…") and `:376-379` ("The following doesn't fully address Bill Pugh's concerns…"); `basic/dimensions.tex:244-254`, Guy's explanation that unit information is static and is omitted from the run-time representation exactly when type information is; `basic/conversions-coercions.tex:19-37`, an open-questions list for coercion including tests, tuple and arrow types; `basic/traits.tex:174-182` and `:195-197`, Victor's observation that a trait can explicitly extend itself through hidden type variables.

`Specification/appendices/internal-document.tex` is the spec's own rationale appendix, included only in draft builds, and it inputs two files: `appendices/FAQ.tex` (235 lines of answered design questions — why multiple dispatch rather than single, `:59`; why spawn counts as IO, `:51`; core versus standard library, `:121`; why not single inheritance between objects, `:136`; juxtaposition as the only non-ALLCAPS operator name, `:90`) and `appendices/future.tex` (756 lines of proposed features organised as Syntax and Evaluation, Types, Traits and Objects, Functions and Overloading, Expressions, Operators and Coercions, Exceptions, Components and APIs, Others, Tools — largely a digest of meetings and emails, with the participants named and their positions recorded, e.g. the array/tensor discussion at `:63-76`).

The formal apparatus is the fourth form: `Specification/appendices/calculi/` holds four core calculi (basic, `where`, overloading, acffd — `appendices/calculi/calculi.tex:18-21`), and `appendices/overloading-function.tex:12` and `appendices/overloading-coercion.tex:12` are the proofs that the overloading rules admit no ambiguous or undefined call, and that coercion resolution is well defined.

`Specification-1.0-frozen/appendices/FAQ.tex` and `future.tex` are byte-identical to the draft's (diff), so the frozen tree adds nothing here; what differs is that the release build hides them.

`Documentation/Specification/` is a second, later, partial spec source tree in Fortify `.tick` form (build instructions at `Documentation/Specification/Prose/README.txt:12-24`, directory roles at `Documentation/Specification/README.txt:13-25`), carrying 35 `\note{}` passages of its own; its committed render `Documentation/Specification/fortress.pdf` is 65 pages, built 2012-05-31, against the draft tree's 599.

Prose documents that state design, not usage: `Fortify/fortify-doc.txt` (489 lines, the Emacs-based ASCII-to-typeset conversion and the identifier-to-symbol rules) with `Fortify/example/README`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/parser-doc.txt` (98 lines, the Rats! module structure of the grammar, with NYI markers); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/syntax_abstractions/productionsAndAst.txt` (127 lines, which productions a user grammar may extend — "Only those marked \"x\" can be extended currently"); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser_util/precedence_resolver/operators.txt` (1,093 lines, the operator groups by meaning and shape that the precedence relation is built from); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/README` (the linker's purpose and file-by-file map); `BasicCoreFortress/README.txt` (how to run the core-calculus interpreter); root `README.txt` (the Subversion-era orientation, describing a project layout that no longer holds).

Long comments that explain a design choice rather than a mechanism, found by scanning every `/* … */` block of 14 lines or more under `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/{compiler,scala_src,runtimeSystem,interpreter}`: `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:26-35` (why a task is not forked in its constructor — "Given the plethora of final fields in the usual Fortress task, such a step would be a memory model disaster!"); `compiler/NamingCzar.java:264-289` (the six-level ladder from a Fortress name to an ASM type, and the two translations needed for foreign interfaces); `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:869-906` (why forwarding methods are generated for every trait after the first, and the normalized-inheritance assumption it rests on), `:1015-1049`, `:1147-1183`, `:2313-2340`, `:5161-5196` (RTTI classes); `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:53-56` ("This code steals willy-nilly from the NextGen class loader"), `:532-552`, `:690-721`, `:935-957` (how arrow and tuple interfaces are synthesized on demand), `:1181-1202`; `runtimeSystem/Naming.java:13-16` (why this class must not depend on the compiler); `runtimeSystem/InstantiationMap.java:195-224` (the name-rewriting state machine); `interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:31-68` ("This comment is not yet true; it is a goal."); `interpreter/evaluator/transactions/manager/KarmaManager.java:17-37` and `EruptionManager.java:17-42` (two of eleven contention-management policies, each with its heuristic explained).

Only one comment in the whole source tree uses the word "rationale" (`interpreter/glue/prim/Reflect.java:333`), and only four say "we chose / we decided / the reason" in any form (`interpreter/evaluator/transactions/manager/FortressManager5.java:22`, `interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:849`, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:2206`, plus the Reflect one); intent in this tree is expressed as mechanism, and 556 `TODO` markers carry what is left of the "not yet" record.

The aspirational test directories are themselves a statement of intent — what was meant to work and did not: `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet` (62 files, e.g. `WhereConstraints.fss`, `UnitExpr.fss`, `Expr.Array.Pasting.fss`, `XXXextendOprParam1.fss`), `long_term_not_working` (6: abstract, closures, fields, inheritance, overriding, wordcount), `not_working_static_tests` (43), `not_working_library_tests` (29), `not_working_compiler_tests` (10), `obsolete_interpreter_tests` (3).

Commit messages: sampled with `git log --grep` over the historical era (`--until=2013-01-01`), they are overwhelmingly implementation logs, and design statements appear in them only in passing — the clearest samples are `128f313b5` (2009-11-17, jmaessen: coercion of `IntLiteral` by `ZZ32`, "as we gradually migrate to a flat numeric hierarchy"), `8e3968ea7` (2009-11-11, skilpat: coercions from union types "as per Guy's blog post" — the blog post is not in the repo), `c35aac139` (2012-04-24, David Chase: "Preliminary disabling of contravariance (in overloaded dispatch)", the retreat the JuliaCon deck describes at slide 44), `32153798d` (2008-04-27, jmaessen: a juxtaposition/type-inference fix that "opened a rift in space-time"), `821e29621` (2008-02-07: BIG operators implemented, "'BIG juxtaposition' is PROD not PRODUCT").

Caveat on that sampling: path-scoped history is unreliable in this repository — `research/authorship.md:14-22` records that the hg→git conversion severed 146 parent links, so `git log -- <path>` dead-ends (it reports one commit for `Papers/`), while `git log --full-history --all -- <path>` over-reports (404 commits for `Papers/`, most of which do not touch it). The `--grep` samples above walk all commits and are sound as samples; they are not an exhaustive search.

## Not verified

Whether the four buildable papers still build today: the PDFs in the tree were built during the revival (`414b790e3`, 2026-08-21) and no build was re-run for this survey.

`Papers/Implementation`: that its two `.tex` files compile under lualatex with the required fonts was not tested; what is verified is that the makefile's source file `FortressEncodings.tex` is absent from the tree and from the tracked history, so `make` cannot succeed as shipped.

Publication venues and years for `Papers/Dispatch` and `Papers/Types`: neither title page states a year; the POPL 2011 and OOPSLA 2011 attributions above come from the reviewer-response file, the committed `SteelePOPL2011.pdf` filename, and `Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:61`. No external source was fetched to confirm them.

`research/README.md` entries not opened here: the JAOO 2008 talk, the April 2005 Sun deck, the ICFP 2009 / Strange Loop 2010 / OOPSLA 1998 adjacent canon. Their coverage is reported as the index describes it, not as read.

`research/decks/` contents are a per-session local state; the two Fortress PDFs are present in this container, but that says nothing about any other session.

The email threads the spec's notes point at (27 of them), Guy's blog post cited by commit `8e3968ea7`, and the `AnySizeArrays` wiki page cited by `appendices/FAQ.tex:57` were not searched for; `research/README.md:110-113` records that mailing-list archives were not found in the 2026-08-21 sweep, and Wayback is unreachable from this container.

The commit-message sample is a sample: nine `--grep` terms, historical era only, and path-scoped history in this repository is broken in both directions (`research/authorship.md:14-22`).

The long-comment scan covered `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/{compiler,scala_src,runtimeSystem,interpreter}` and blocks of 14 lines or more; shorter comments carrying intent, and other source roots, were not scanned.

Whether `Documentation/Specification/`'s `.tick` prose differs substantively from `Specification/`'s LaTeX was not diffed; only its size, build date and note count were checked.

## Decisions not made

Whether `Papers/Implementation` should be made buildable — the missing `FortressEncodings.tex` could be reconstructed as a wrapper around the two existing documents, but that is an edit inside the sealed tree and is the owner's call.

Whether the specification's draft-only apparatus (the `\note{}` boxes and the Internal Document appendix) should be surfaced as a first-class revival document, given that it is the richest rationale source in the repository and is invisible to anyone reading the published 1.0 PDF.

Whether to pursue the lost email record — the 27 named threads are the primary rationale source for coercion, overloading, arrays, tuples, fairness and function equality, and recovering even one thread would change what several rows above can say.

Whether `research/README.md` should index the two APL deck files now sitting in `research/decks/`, which belong to a different line of work.

Whether the aspirational test directories (`not_passing_yet`, `long_term_not_working`, and the three `not_working_*`) should be read as a design-intent source in their own right and cross-referenced to the gap ledger.

Ten-line summary:
1. Five rationale places: `Papers/`, the corpus indexed by `research/README.md`, `research/extracts/`, the spec's draft-only apparatus, and the source tree (tool docs, long comments, aspirational test dirs, commit messages).
2. `Papers/` holds five directories; Dispatch, Types (+ Types/journal), Welterweight and RuntimeInstantiation all build and their PDFs were committed in the revival (`414b790e3`); titles, authors and stated venues are cited per file:line.
3. `Papers/Implementation` (TypeMapping.tex, MethodMapping.tex — the JVM encoding, "the meaning and rationale behind the design") does **not** build as shipped: its makefile's only source, `FortressEncodings.tex`, is absent from the tree and from the tracked history; the committed render dates from 2011-02-07.
4. The specification's rationale is draft-only: 230 `\note{}` boxes plus the Internal Document appendix (FAQ.tex + future.tex) are suppressed by `\ifrelease`; "Internal Document" appears 0 times in the published 1.0 PDF and twice in the in-repo 599-page draft render, which also carries 36 "Victor:" editorial notes the 1.0 PDF lacks. The word "rationale" occurs once in the whole LaTeX, about component upgrade.
5. The deepest layer is missing: 27 notes point at Sun-internal email threads by subject and date, and `research/README.md:103-105` records no mailing-list archive was ever found.
6. `research/decks/` is non-empty in this container (JuliaCon 2016 and Growing a Syntax PDFs present, plus two unindexed APL files); JAOO 2008, the April 2005 deck, Four Solutions and the adjacent canon are link-only. Availability is reported per item as a session state, not a repo state.
7. The four extracts are mapped to what design intent each records, with line cites (JuliaCon principles/algebraic traits/where-it-broke; Four Solutions' "wiggle room"; Growing a Syntax; the wind-down post's eight pleased-with and three wished-explored-further).
